haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup in step 7, before readiness. GET /healthz returns 503 until all three keys are loaded, then 200, so the instance takes traffic only after loading.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the fetch (1 attempt plus up to 3 retries, 2s apart), then logs the secret name and error type and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, so the rollout halts and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes the app re-reads each secret. If the version id changed, it swaps in the new pair. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and does not restart or return 503.
haiku-low.q4: Values are held in process memory, in a map in app/secrets.py, never on disk. They must never appear in logs, exception messages, crash output, environment variables, or logged HTTP headers. The version endpoint shows ids only.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod identity can read prod keys, read-only, and only the security on-call can write them. No engineer group has any access to prod.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys stay in git history permanently, so they must be rotated at the providers. Old values become harmless only when revoked at the provider in step 14, after every instance is confirmed on new keys.
haiku-low.q7: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__. At each outgoing request they call secrets.get(name) to read the current in-memory value.
haiku-low.q8: Step 13: every pod runs the new image, each pod's version endpoint reports the validated latest version id for all three secrets, provider dashboards show no old-key use, and other consumers have moved.
haiku-low.q9: Plan order: set store access (step 2), rotate at providers (4), validate and write keys to store (5), switch app and remove file keys in one change deployed (6-12), revoke old keys (14). The question's order is not the plan's.
haiku-low.q10: make run uses APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* with the engineer's own credentials. Those secrets hold provider test keys. make run-offline uses local fakes and needs no key.
haiku-low.q11: It logs the missing secret's name and error type, never a value, and exits non-zero. A partial load never counts as success, so the pod restarts and never becomes ready.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first at startup (all three, step 7). Readiness (/healthz) returns 503 until all three are loaded, then 200.
sonnet.q2: It retries (1 attempt + 3 retries, 2s apart), logs secret name and error type, and exits non-zero; it is restarted and never becomes ready. The rollout halts (maxUnavailable: 0) and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer every 5 minutes re-reads each secret independently; if the version id changed, it swaps in the new value/version and logs it. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (name, error type, current version id), and does not restart or return 503; alert if warnings repeat.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory only, in a map of name to (value, version id) in app/secrets.py, replaced as a whole. They must never be on disk, in environment variables, or in any log line, exception message or crash output (including HTTP request headers).
sonnet.q5: Read: the orders-api-prod identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Write: only the security on-call. Ordinary engineers have no prod read or write.
sonnet.q6: The old keys remain in git history permanently. That is why every key is rotated at its provider; the old keys are revoked (step 14) after all instances are confirmed on the new ones, which makes the leaked values dead.
sonnet.q7: The map in app/secrets.py is replaced with the new pair; each client (Payments, Email, Geocoding) calls secrets.get("<name>") at each outgoing request rather than storing the key in __init__, so the next request uses the new value.
sonnet.q8: Step 13: all running pods listed from the cluster run the new image; every pod's version endpoint (queried one by one from inside the cluster) reports the latest store version id for all three secrets, matching an id validated in step 5; provider dashboards show no recent old-key use where available; other consumers from the step 1 inventory have moved. Any mismatch means do not revoke.
sonnet.q9: Store access set up (step 2); new keys created at providers, i.e. rotated (step 4); validated and copied into the store (step 5); app code switched to read from the store and keys removed from the committed file in the same change (steps 6-11); deploy (12); confirm (13); then old keys revoked (14). Only the order of 4 vs 2 is fixed as 2 before 4.
sonnet.q10: From orders-api/dev/* in the store (provider test keys), via make run with APP_ENV=dev, using the engineer's own credentials. make run-offline uses local fakes and needs no key.
sonnet.q11: It treats it as failure: logs the secret name and error type, exits non-zero (no partial load), is restarted, and never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided whether or how often; the plan picks no cadence.
